# 20-configuration.md — SECTION 3 SOURCE: CONFIGURATION, IDENTITY AND SKILL COMPOSITION
This section is the CHD-3.5 configuration projection. **The adopted v4 contract in `contracts/config.schema.json` and `build-spec/integrated/config-format.md` owns field names, types, limits, defaults, absence semantics, precedence, activation and errors.** The generated field inventory is subordinate evidence. Historical v2/v3 spellings are migration input only and never deployment input. If an older projection differs, this v4 contract governs; the discrepancy is recorded rather than guessed away.
## C.1 Desired and effective configuration

### C.1.1 One desired document and the projections read from it A deployment has one VP/operator-owned **desired** configuration, but four readable scopes: - **Project:** instruction roots, a project config reference and the optional project-memory route. Multiple absolute instruction/workspace roots are supported; project prose cannot grant a capability. - **Agent:** role, skills, tools, grants, approvals, runtime, rooms, limits and composition selection. - **Host/gateway:** gateway identity, transport, workdir, credential *reference* and profiles enrolled on that host. A host binds an agent to a gateway; it does not become the agent's identity. - **Profile:** the named Hermes profile, credential reference, session/memory scope and managed asset inventory. It is stateful and attributable, not a host sandbox.

### C.1.2 Four independent version domains The four version domains are independent and are not interchangeable. The configuration document is **schema v4**; controller records (registry, provisioning, manifests and audit records) are **record schema v3**; the content-addressed asset bundle manifest is **bundle v1**; and the transport operation envelope is **`chd.operation.v1`**. The archive manifest is **archive manifest v1** and its native Hermes payload version is a probed value. The canonical compatibility and migration table is `tables/section-4-version-matrix.csv`; a record never reuses a config or transport version number. TABLE 3.1-2 — THE FOUR VERSION DOMAINS AND THEIR IDENTIFIERS | Version domain | Identifier | What it versions | |---|---|---| | Configuration document | `schema v4` | the desired configuration document | | Controller records | `record schema v3` | registry, provisioning, manifests and audit records | | Asset bundle | `bundle v1` | the content-addressed asset bundle manifest | | Transport operation envelope | `chd.operation.v1` | the operation envelope | | Archive manifest | `archive manifest v1` | the archive manifest; its native Hermes payload version is a probed value |

A record never reuses a config or transport version number. The canonical compatibility and migration table is `tables/section-4-version-matrix.csv`.

### C.1.3 Effective readback and the absence rule `GET /v1/effective-config/{agent-id}` returns the desired and profile-reported effective revisions, digests, every resolved field, `drifted`, provenance and a source reference. It must read the profile's current report, not a cached desired copy. Session-scoped policy readback names its frozen revision and must match its snapshot byte-for-byte (VOL-D VOLD-006). A missing optional field is not an implied value. Each field is `REQUIRED-EXPLICIT`, `EXPLICIT-DEFAULT` (only where VOL-D names a source value), or carried v2 `REQUIRED`. The registry records the class's omission meaning as `default_or_unresolved`; `UNRESOLVED` means the loader refuses absence. Schema defaults are documentation/readback defaults, never a license to invent one. Credentials are references such as `/chd/credentials/agent-a`, never tokens or secret values. TABLE 3.1-3 — FIELD CLASSES AND WHAT ABSENCE MEANS | Field class | Omission meaning | Loader behaviour | |---|---|---| | `REQUIRED-EXPLICIT` | `default_or_unresolved` | absence is refused unless a VOL-D source value exists | | `EXPLICIT-DEFAULT` | `default_or_unresolved` | only where VOL-D names a source value | | carried v2 `REQUIRED` | — | carried for compatibility; same refusal rule | | `UNRESOLVED` | `default_or_unresolved` | the loader refuses absence | | credential reference | — | a reference such as `/chd/credentials/agent-a`, never a token or secret value |

A missing optional field is not an implied value. Schema defaults are documentation and readback defaults, never a license to invent one.
## C.2 Runtime settings and native fallback

### C.2.1 Runtime values are carried verbatim, never negotiated `runtime.provider`, `runtime.model` and `runtime.context_window` are explicit per agent/worker. `max_turns` and `token_budget` are pass-through values when supplied. CHD sends these values verbatim to Hermes; `context_window` is a ceiling. CHD does not compact history or reconstruct context. Hermes owns native fallback behavior. CHD records a reported fallback in the send manifest/readback but does not define a fallback provider/model, retry policy, health table or rerouting algorithm. A provider failure never authorizes CHD to reroute. TABLE 3.2-1 — RUNTIME FIELDS, DECLARER AND TREATMENT | Runtime field | Declared by | CHD treatment | |---|---|---| | `runtime.provider` | agent/worker, explicitly | sent verbatim to Hermes | | `runtime.model` | agent/worker, explicitly | sent verbatim to Hermes | | `runtime.context_window` | agent/worker, explicitly | a ceiling; CHD does not compact or reconstruct history | | `max_turns` | agent/worker, when supplied | pass-through value | | `token_budget` | agent/worker, when supplied | pass-through value | | fallback provider and model | Hermes | not defined by CHD; a reported fallback is recorded in the send manifest and readback | | retry policy, health table, rerouting | Hermes | outside CHD; a provider failure never authorizes rerouting |

## C.3 Identity, profile isolation, and effective readback (R32-004)
Every director, manager, supervisor, foreman and worker has a distinct `(principal_id, profile_id)` binding. The binding is explicit in the desired configuration and in every effective readback; it is never derived from a role, room sender, host name, diagram, or skill. `profile_id` is a lower-case stable identifier and MUST NOT be `default`; `principal_id`, `agent_id`, `host_id`, `room_id`, `thread_root`, `work_uid`, `bond_id`, `parent_bond_id`, and `session_id` each have their own typed field and constrained identifier grammar. The validator rejects omission (`profile_missing`), `default` (`profile_not_distinct`) and reuse (`profile_shared`) before a run record is created. A host may enroll several profiles, but it does not become the principal and does not merge their session, credential, learned, or archive state.
The profile contract is `schemas/profile-identity.schema.json`. It requires the profile's principal, role, host/gateway binding, credential reference, separate session-state root, learned-state reference, and protected learned-state policy. `learned_state_ref` is a reference only: CHD may identify and protect it, but Hermes owns learning, recall, history, compaction, and memory semantics. A configuration sync may replace managed assets and settings only; it MUST NOT copy, delete, overwrite, or reinterpret learned state, session history, or archives. The grantor-without-use case remains valid: a profile can have `grant_use` without `use`; no profile identity or role name fills the missing class.
`GET /v1/effective-config/{agent-id}` returns the schema in `schemas/effective-profile-readback.schema.json`: desired and effective revisions/digests, the fully resolved identity/profile/host/room bindings, policy owner, provenance for every field, protected-state references, drift, and the readback source. The response MUST be generated from the profile's current report, not a desired-config cache. Equal-revision differing bytes are an integrity error. A diagram, sender, parent bond, or transport peer is never a policy-owner source; `policy_owner` is an explicit constrained principal reference and omission is invalid.

### C.3.1 Configuration and effective-readback field contract
TABLE 3.1-1 — C.3.1 Configuration and effective-readback field contract
| Field | Type / constraint | Meaning and authority | |---|---|---| | `principal_id` | string, `^pr-[a-z0-9-]+$` | Authenticated role identity; controller binds it to the request. | | `profile_id` | string, `^pf-[a-z0-9-]+$`, not `default` | Named Hermes profile; unique per principal/instance. | | `host_id` | string, `^host-[a-z0-9-]+$` | Enrolled host reference; never an authority or principal alias. | | `role` | enum `director\|manager\|supervisor\|foreman\|worker` | Configured role; role text cannot grant capability. | | `credential_ref` | non-empty reference, `^/chd/credentials/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$` | Secret locator only; secret bytes are forbidden. | | `session_state_ref` | non-empty reference, `^/chd/session-state/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$` | Profile-owned native session state. | | `learned_state_ref` | non-empty reference, `^/chd/learned-state/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$` | Protected Hermes-owned learning/recall state. | | `room_id` | string, `^(obj\|task\|space)-[a-z0-9-]+$` | Explicit room binding; membership is not authority. | | `thread_root` | positive integer | Explicit message root for a branch. | | `work_uid` | string, `^work-[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$` | Logical work identity; never inferred from latest session. | | `policy_owner` | string, `^pr-[a-z0-9-]+$` | Explicit VP/operator policy principal; never inferred from diagrams or senders. | | `effective_revision` | positive integer | Gateway/profile-reported revision read back after convergence. | | `effective_digest` | string, `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$` | Digest of the effective document, not desired bytes. |
The controller fails closed on unknown fields, null-as-absent substitutions, missing required bindings, cross-profile collisions, digest mismatch, or a readback whose `principal_id`, `profile_id`, `host_id`, or `policy_owner` does not match the desired binding. It never silently substitutes the default profile or current sender.

### C.3.2 Same-profile native fork versus cross-profile assignment A same-profile fork is a native Hermes fork only when the parent and child have the same explicit `instance`, `profile_id`, and host capability binding. It retains D-038 semantics: the child records `parent_bond_id`, `parent_session_id`, `fork_point_seq`, and explicit `fork_mode`; the default is `preserve_parent_snapshot`, with `current_policy` as the explicit alternative. The child is delivered as `NEW`; later branch replies use `REUSE`. A cross-profile or cross-host handoff is **not** a native fork and is not represented as `provisioning: fork`. It is a new assignment requiring an explicit `context_transfer_request` and an adapter capability probe for the selected source/target pair. The request names source and target principal, profile, host, room, thread root, work UID, parent bond/session, policy owner, selected archive/checkpoint references, and an import mode. The adapter may return an imported reference or a typed error, but it cannot copy sender authority, credentials, policy snapshots, or learned state. No native cross-profile fork is claimed unless the probe explicitly returns `cross_profile_native_fork: true`; absent, stale, or negative probe means `cross_profile_native_fork_unsupported` and the controller creates no child session. The transfer target receives only the explicitly authorized context import. It must resolve its own current policy and create its own `SessionPolicySnapshot`; source authority and source `policy_owner` are not inherited. The transfer request/result/error records are defined in `schemas/context-transfer-{request,result,error}.schema.json` and are all read back before success. `policy_owner` is carried as an explicit reference for audit and authorization; it is never guessed from a figure, room sender, or parent bond.
## C.4 One composition authority and two conflict planes

### C.4.1 One composition authority, three ordered inputs
There is one composition authority, VOL-D VOLD-017–VOLD-019:
1. **Project/workspace instructions** are read by Hermes from the selected scope. 2. **Base role template** is selected by `composition.base_role`. 3. **Named specialization** is selected by `composition.specialization.name`.
CHD selects the asset list and authorized boundaries; Hermes composes behavior. A specialization can override only named `authorized_overrides` values (`behavior` and/or `permissions`), and a permissions delta must remain inside the VP-configured pool.

### C.4.2 Two conflict planes that never cross The conflict planes are not interchangeable. Permission conflict is a hard validation/grant-time failure. An instruction contradiction fails as `specialization_conflict` unless behavior override is explicitly authorized; when authorized, the named specialization wins over the base role only within that authorization. Neither plane can outrank VP configuration. Skill text, prompt text, skill membership or a task assignment is instruction/context, not an actual grant. Use, grant-use, confer-delegation and create remain independent; “I may send” in a skill does not create a grant.
## C.5 Precedence and the VP denial worked example

### C.5.1 The fixed precedence order
For effective permission resolution, the fixed order is **VP configuration → director on-demand delegation → named specialization override → base role**. This is the single precedence authority in VOL-D; other sections reference it. Project instructions are the first composition layer but cannot grant authority. VP-configured permissions are already grants and need no director grant (D-016). A lower layer cannot turn a VP denial into an allow.

### C.5.2 Worked readback: a director grant that the VP denial outranks Worked readback for `room:task-crier`: TABLE 3.5-1 — TWO DOCUMENTS, ONE DENIAL | Document | Recorded path | Value | Status | |---|---|---|---| | VP desired config, revision 41 | `vp.grants.room_read` | `agents: [sup-crier]`; `rooms: []` — the VP denies this room scope | effective | | Director request | `chd/grants/grant-204` | `origin: director`, `granted_by: mgr-infra`, `capability: room_read`, `scope: room:task-crier` | `recorded_conflict` | TABLE 3.5-2 — EFFECTIVE READBACK FOR AGENT `sup-crier` | Readback field | Value | |---|---| | `agent` | `sup-crier` | | `field` | `permissions.use.room_read[room:task-crier]` | | `value` | `denied` | | `origin` | `vp_configured` | | `source_ref` | `/chd/config/desired/rev/41/vp/grants/room_read` | | `lower_precedence` | `director:grant-204` | | `resolution` | `vp_wins` | | `audit` | `grant_conflict` | The director record remains provenance-bearing audit history; it is not silently rewritten and does not become an effective grant. The denial is checked again at grant time and in effective readback.
## C.6 Validation, update, activation and readback

### C.6.1 The loader is four gates and fails closed The loader runs **schema → referential integrity → policy → warnings** and fails closed on any error. Unknown fields are errors at every object level; `additionalProperties: false` is intentional. Referential checks bind gateway, room, registry, worker-target and profile references. Policy checks enforce profile uniqueness, permission-key exclusivity, grant bounds, specialization authorization and complete explicit temporary-worker fields. Warnings never convert an error to a load.

### C.6.2 What changes when, and what readback must show
VP/operator changes bindings, caps, triggers, room membership, approval policy, specialization assets and desired config through the validated path. Directors may issue only on-demand grants inside the VP-approved pool. Agents cannot edit their binding, skills, grants or membership. Activation follows VOL-D VOLD-008: caps/membership at the next orchestrator check; triggers at scheduler registration; runtime, tools, skills and approval policy at the next new or reused session turn; in-flight sends retain their dispatch-time digest. Readback shows the new revision or no change, never partial convergence as success.
## C.7 Managed-template sync and learned state

### C.7.1 The sync procedure `chd_profile_sync` is a procedure, not a promise: 1. Read desired config and the profile's effective report. Verify profile identity, revisions, digests and asset manifest before writing. 2. Compute a field/asset diff. Managed state is configuration, tools, skills, prompts and small content-addressed assets. Learned memory, session history and archived work are **not** in the replacement set. 3. Update settings and upload changed assets in the VOL-D order. Retain the prior effective revision and replacement manifest for rollback. 4. Read back inventory (name, version, sha256), runtime and settings; run a smoke turn under the same named profile. Presence alone is not verification. 5. Publish effective revision/digest, drift state, lineage and readback origin. Only then is the profile dispatchable.

### C.7.2 Failure, retry and rollback
If upload, digest, readiness or smoke-turn verification fails, retain the prior effective revision, emit `converge_failed` with the failed step, and do not claim partial readiness. Retry from the recorded diff; rollback restores the prior desired digest and repeats readback. Sync never deletes or replaces learned state. Cleanup waits for terminal work and archive checkpoint verification, then records old/new profile and archive references.
## C.8 Temporary agents

### C.8.1 The explicit field set, with no invented defaults
Temporary workers are a supported explicit-input path. The request must provide every field in TABLE 3.8-1; the controller rejects any missing field as `temporary_field_missing{path}`.
TABLE 3.8-1 — THE FIFTEEN EXPLICIT FIELDS OF A TEMPORARY WORKER
| Field | Requirement | |---|---| | `temporary` | `true` | | `worker_id` | unique | | `work_uid` | required | | `profile` | non-default | | `gateway` | required | | `credential_ref` | required | | `model` | required | | `context_window` | required | | `max_turns` | required | | `token_budget` | required | | `lifetime` | required | | `workspace` | required | | `asset_bundle_ref` | required | | `archive_policy` | required | | `capacity_class` | required |
It never invents the unsettled provider, context, lifetime, workspace or capacity defaults. Proposed defaults remain an owner-scoped record (`OPEN-VOLD-1`) and do not disable explicit workers.

### C.8.2 The ten-step lifecycle is mandatory The lifecycle is complete and mandatory: reserve capacity and write the provisioning record; install/probe the credential; create and read back the unique profile; stage assets/settings and read them back; execute the named work unit through controller-brokered dispatch; ingest one report; commit an archive checkpoint; then retire, revoke and read back the retired registry. A temporary worker is dispatchable only after all provisioning/readiness gates pass. Each step is read back before the next one is allowed to run: the reservation and provisioning record are read back before the credential is installed and probed, the profile is created and read back before assets and settings are staged, the staged assets are read back before the named work unit executes, one report is ingested before the archive checkpoint is committed, and the retired registry is read back after revocation. A step that cannot be read back blocks the step after it, which is why a temporary worker is never "partly" dispatchable and never inherits a default for a field the request left out. A lost create response is reconciled by `GET` using the same request identity before retry; a lost run/report is reconciled by the run manifest and report readback. A failure before retirement leaves `temporary_retire_pending` and holds capacity until terminal execution and archive evidence are proven. The explicit path is not equivalent to implicit defaults: the unsupported input is only an omitted required field, not the temporary-worker feature itself.
## C.9 Fixtures and checks

### C.9.1 The two checks and what each must report
The complete examples are in `examples/config/`. Both checks are required.
TABLE 3.9-1 — CHECKS AND THEIR REQUIRED RESULTS
| Command | Required result | |---|---| | `python3 handbook/chd32/scripts/validate_config.py --cross-check` | zero missing registry rows | | `python3 handbook/chd32/scripts/validate_config.py handbook/chd32/examples/config/valid-full.yaml` | the full example validates |

### C.9.2 Named failure fixtures The invalid fixtures fail with their named machine errors, and each error names the contract rule it enforces (TABLE 3.9-2). Each named error is a refusal, not a warning: a fixture passes only when the loader rejects the input with that exact name, and a warning can never downgrade the refusal into a load. The four fixtures therefore walk the C.6 gates in the order they run - closed objects, referential resolution, policy exclusivity, and the explicit temporary-worker field set - so a green run says something about the loader rather than about the fixture's spelling. TABLE 3.9-2 — INVALID FIXTURES AND THE RULE EACH ENFORCES | Machine error | Rule enforced | |---|---| | `unknown_field` | unknown fields are errors at every object level (`additionalProperties: false`) | | `profile_missing` | the profile reference must resolve | | `permission_key_conflict` | permission-key exclusivity in the policy pass | | `temporary_field_missing` | every explicit temporary-worker field must be present | A temporary worker with all explicit fields is valid; only omitted required fields are rejected. `contracts/config.schema.json` is the bundled v4 structural contract. Unknown fields fail at every closed object level. `schema_version` MUST be integer `4`; 2, 3, absent and future versions fail before any write, provisioning or trigger registration. A v2/v3 document is not silently upgraded: migration emits an operator-reviewed old/new diff, maps legacy locations explicitly, rejects both old and new spellings appearing together, and validates a complete v4 document before effects. `runtime.provider`, `runtime.model`, `runtime.context_window`, `runtime.max_turns` and `runtime.token_budget` are the exact v4 names; the old `context_limit` and flat agent runtime keys are not accepted aliases. The v4 precedence is exact: VP configuration, then valid director delegation, then valid manager delegation, with explicit deny winning over lower-layer allow; project instructions cannot grant authority. Fork maps are VP-authored choices, not an ordered strictness lattice: project choices must agree, then project precedes agent, then global. The default is `preserve_parent_snapshot`; `current_policy` is an explicit authorized alternative. Restore is different: `session.restore_policy` is `current_policy` on every restore. Archived policy remains history only; source and effective revisions are stored separately, and a missing archived source revision is `null`/unknown, never fabricated. Existing live sessions retain their bound snapshot and never auto-resync. Temporary workers are supported only with complete explicit inputs. Missing fields fail as `temporary_field_missing{path}`; no model, provider, lifetime, privilege, workspace, retention or capacity default is invented. A fully explicit worker is not rejected merely because unresolved implicit defaults remain OPEN. **References:** VOL-D §1 (VOLD-001–VOLD-021, VOLD-064–VOLD-074), VOL-C §12, D-015, D-016, R31-020, R31-025, F-005 and F-012.
